1.e4 d5 2.exd5 Nf6 3.d4 Nxd5 4.c4.strategy: Drives the knight away with a gain of time and builds a broad centre. Black must retreat the knight and fight for a share of it; White gets a space advantage, at the price of a slightly shut-in f1-bishop and a c4 pawn that becomes a target.

1.e4 d5 2.exd5 Nf6 3.d4 Nxd5 4.Nf3.strategy: Develops and defends d4, choosing piece development over chasing the knight at once. The pawn push to c4 can follow, but meanwhile Black has time to develop the c8-bishop outside the pawn chain.

1.e4 d5 2.exd5 Nf6 3.d4 Nxd5 4.c4 Nb4.strategy: A speculative try: the knight hits c2 and d3, hoping for Qa4+ N8c6 d5? b5! with a good game. But White simply drives it back with a3, gaining time and space, so Black has spent two moves with the same knight for nothing.
1.e4 d5 2.exd5 Nf6 3.d4 Nxd5 4.c4 Nb4.name: Scandinavian Defence: Kiel Variation
1.e4 d5 2.exd5 Nf6 3.d4 Nxd5 4.c4 Nb4.background: Rarely seen in practice because it is difficult to play effectively; Harman and Taulbut call it "a speculative try".

1.e4 d5 2.exd5 Nf6 3.d4 Nxd5 4.Nf3 Bg4.strategy: Develops the bishop before it is shut in by ...e6 and pins the f3-knight to the queen, so White's centre loses a defender if the knight is taken. Black aims to catch up in development before White's space tells.
1.e4 d5 2.exd5 Nf6 3.d4 Nxd5 4.Nf3 Bg4.name: Scandinavian Defence: Modern Variation, Gipslis Variation

1.e4 d5 2.exd5 Nf6 3.d4 Nxd5 4.Nf3 g6.strategy: Prepares a fianchetto aimed at d4. White gains time with c4 against the knight on d5 and builds a big centre, while Black has the long-term pressure of the bishop as compensation; sound, but White's space is easy to play with.
1.e4 d5 2.exd5 Nf6 3.d4 Nxd5 4.Nf3 g6.name: Scandinavian Defence: Richter Variation
